Subject: Dedicated capacity validation: StellarHealth SLOs, GPU fit, and next steps

Hi Amit / Procurement team —

Thank you again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned on SLOs and what we’ll validate in a short dedicated-capacity proof-of-fit run. Please correct anything I’ve misstated.

Key product context (from call):
- Use case: clinician-facing assistant that summarizes records and suggests next steps (interactive).
- Typical prompt -> response token size: 40–120 tokens (median ~60).
- Expected active clinician concurrency at launch: ~120 users (peaks to ~200 during rounds).
- Burst pattern: concentrated morning/afternoon windows (10–15 minute bursts).

SLO / perf targets (your asks):
- First-token tail: p99 < 250 ms (streaming-first-token).
- Steady-state per-token latency during streaming: ~< 40 ms/token (p95).
- End-to-end completion for short responses (<=120 tokens): p95 < 650 ms.
- Throughput requirement (reserved): baseline 500 tokens/sec sustained, burstable to 1,200 tokens/sec for 10 minutes.
- Concurrency goal: support 200 concurrent interactive requests with acceptable queuing/backpressure.

What we’ll validate in the dedicated run:
1) GPU fit: H100 vs A100 (and an A10G cost check) with INT8/FP16 quantization profiles where applicable.
2) Prefix/KV caching benefits for repeated clinical templates.
3) Streaming-first-token latency and per-token stability at target concurrency and burst.
4) Failure/fallback behavior under oversubscription and warmup characteristics of KV cache.

Deliverables / next steps from Redwood:
- Proposed test matrix (GPU types x quant levels x concurrency points) + estimated #GPUs needed. (Deliver by EOW Wed 06/24).
- Small benchmark run in our lab with your sample prompts (need your anonymized prompt sample and a small token budget for the run).
- Cost/Pricing sketch for Dedicated pools meeting the reserved throughput profile.

Action items we need from StellarHealth:
- A sanitized sample prompt set (5–10 representative sessions).
- Confirmation of regulatory region preference (you mentioned us-east-1).
- Any hard constraints (e.g., max monthly $ spend, procurement windows).

Attachments: I’ll include a quick SLO calc workbook and our internal GPU comparison matrix in the next email.

Thanks —
Evelyn

Evelyn / Karthik —

Thanks for the context. Below is a proposed short plan and the high-level GPU delta analysis we can send to Amit by EOD. I’ll own the lab runs and the SLO calc workbook.

Proposed test matrix (short, focused):
- Workloads: 60-token median, 120-token worst-case, streaming-first-token microbench.
- Concurrency points: 50, 120, 200 concurrent users (arrival patterns to emulate peak bursts).
- Throughput nodes: validate sustained 500 tps and 1,200 tps 10-minute burst.
- GPUs: H100 (FP16/FP8 if available), A100S (FP16), A10G (INT8 where supported).

Delta analysis (back-of-envelope):
- H100: best-in-class first-token latency for large-context models; expect p99-first-token ~140–200 ms in our runtime at warm cache for 60-token sessions. For sustained 500 tps baseline we estimate 2 H100s (with autoscaling headroom) and for the 1.2k tps burst ~4 H100s with warm prefix caching. Monthly reserved pool estimate (Redwood list rates + reserved premium): ~$55k–72k/mo depending on quant and cache hit rate.
- A100S: ~20–40% slower tail latencies vs H100 on identical model builds; expect p99-first-token ~200–300 ms (warm). Sustained 500 tps likely needs 3 A100S; burst to 1.2k ~6 A100S. Monthly: ~$38k–50k/mo.
- A10G (cost-optimized): latency and quantization tradeoffs; INT8 can reduce memory and increase throughput but p99-first-token may exceed 300–400 ms depending on model and quant errors. Viable for non-tight SLO modes; recommended as fallback tier. Monthly: ~$18k–28k/mo.

Notes / assumptions:
- Estimates assume model is quant-friendly and we can use KV/prefix caching effectively.
- First-token p99 strongly depends on model head-room and KV cache warmness; cold-start behavior will be worse.
- We’ll include measurements for both warm and cold cache in the benchmark.

Deliverables I’ll produce by EOD (Wed 06/23):
- SLO calc workbook populated with the three GPU rows (stellar_slo_calc.xlsx).
- GPU comparison CSV (gpu-comparison-matrix.csv).
- Short lab bench PDF with initial runs (baseline-lab-bench-20260620.pdf).
- A 1-page recommendation (H100 for strict SLO, A100S as price-performance compromise; A10G as cost fallback).

Next actions / owners:
- Rishi: run lab benchmarks + populate workbook (ETA: EOD Wed 06/23).
- Karthik: draft pricing sketch & committed pool options (ETA: Thu 06/24).
- Evelyn: coordinate sample prompt upload & procurement cadence with StellarHealth.

I’ll share the artifacts and a short slide with the recommendation once the runs complete.

—Rishi
